<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-security/CHANGELOG.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 550233855e · card #37563 · area s2-data · 2026-11-27T15:57Z

**L1 checklist** (no review face on this file list past the declaration fallback: this record is the review of record)
- **Shape and checks.** 39 success, 15 expected skip on the head; the one red is `Check Changeset`, by design (below). Prose only, no code: `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/sharing-service.mdx`, the consumed pre changeset `.changeset/pre/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md`, and its published entry in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/CHANGELOG.md`; 54 changed lines, not governed.
- **Item 1, the page.** It now lists `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` with their `SharingWriteVerdict` and `canEdit` / `canDelete` as the two-state projection, and the optional `checkEditMany` / `checkDeleteMany` with the feature-detected per-record fallback. Read against `packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts` on `main`: `canEdit` / `canDelete` are `!== 'deny'` of the tri-state form; a system context is `allow` and a bypass-listed object `abstain` (`bypassVerdict`); no schema, a `public` write OWD or no owner field is `abstain`, no user is `deny`; a failed lookup, of one record or a whole chunk, is `deny` (`writeGateFailClosed`); the chunk is `WRITE_VERDICT_CHUNK = 1000`. Every sentence of the new section matches one of these.
- **Item 2, DELIBERATE CORRECTION.** Changeset 35802 has shipped, so the cost paragraph is corrected in both places it lives, with the same words: the consumed pre note `.changeset/pre/35802-predicate-write-floor-deferral.md` (the stable cut re-applies consumed pre changesets, `scripts/changeset-changelog.mjs`) and its `plugin-security` CHANGELOG entry under 19.0.0-next.0. The seat confirms the correction, sentence by sentence, in each note:
  - Before: "The by-id decision costs one sharing verdict, a few store reads, for each matched row the floor does not already admit. Measured on SQLite in memory:"
  - After: "The by-id decision is one sharing verdict for each matched row the floor does not already admit. The bundled sharing service (`@objectstack/plugin-sharing`) answers all of them through its set form, `checkEditMany` / `checkDeleteMany`, in chunks of 1,000 rows: one read of the chunk's rows and, for an update, one read of the caller's write-level shares on them, so the store reads grow per 1,000 rows rather than per row. Measured on SQLite over 10,000 rows owned by another user: a member's predicate update takes 24 store reads and about 0.27 s, the same delete 13 reads, and a Modify All holder's update of all 10,000 rows 14 reads, and it now writes those rows." and "A sharing service that does not implement the set form is asked `checkEdit` / `checkDelete` once per row, 25 at a time, with the same answers, and then each verdict costs a few store reads. Measured on SQLite in memory with the per-row form:"
  - The figures are PR #37558's measured table (24 reads · 270 ms, 13 reads, 14 reads over 10,000 rows) and its changeset's "25 at a time"; the per-row bullets below the paragraph are unchanged and now read as the per-row form, which they measured.
- **Designed red.** `Check Changeset` is red by design on this class (route 0, ruling D, #18375; `check-empty-changeset.mjs` and the `pr-automation.yml` comment say so on the pushed branch), the workflow runs on `pull_request` only, not `merge_group`, and this record names the gate and its cause, so the PR is queued with that red standing. No `skip-changeset`, rightly.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Fixes #37563` is right: both items are done.

Tier: S. Landing: ready and auto-merge in this stroke.
